channel.title: Lyceum Shorts
channel.description: Short educational films that ship their own source.

item.title: A cube cut into eight blocks
item.description: Derivation: A cube of side a + b, cut at a along each edge, falls into eight blocks (one a³, three a²b, three ab², one b³), so (a + b)³ = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³ for positive lengths a and b.

item.title: Why cells are small
item.description: Demonstration: For cubes, surface area divided by volume is 6, 3 and 2 for sides 1, 2 and 3, falling as 1 / side, so a bigger cell has less surface for each bit of interior.

item.title: Hardy–Weinberg as a square
item.description: Demonstration: With random mating, one generation of offspring comes in the proportions p² + 2pq + q², drawn as a square, and the allele frequencies p and q are unchanged afterwards.

item.title: A crank, a rod and a piston
item.description: Demonstration: In a crank-slider the piston reaches its dead centers at the ends of the stroke, and the leverage of a steady push on the piston vanishes there and is largest near the middle of the stroke.

item.title: Two motions at once
item.description: Demonstration: A thrown ball's path is two independent motions: constant horizontal speed, and vertical motion under constant gravity.

item.title: Squares on a right triangle
item.description: Demonstration: On a right triangle, the squares on the two legs together cover exactly the square on the hypotenuse: 3² + 4² = 5², shown with tiles, then again for 5-12-13 and 8-15-17.
